name: HEICO Corporation
businessSummary: Aerospace, defense and electronics products/services via Flight Support Group (jet engine/aircraft replacement parts, insulation, repair services) and Electronic Technologies Group.

price.note: An earlier forecast-page fetch (2026-10-23) showed $297.36 -- unreconciled ~12% discrepancy; ratios below use the Oct 23 figure and may understate current valuation.

marketCap.note: Ratios page (Oct 23) cited $41,558M, reflecting the price discrepancy.

netDebt.note: Actual net debt (not cash); FY2025 net debt ~$2,694M.

fcfYield.note: FY2025 was 2.25% -- low given the multiple.

payoutRatio.note: ~4-5% of EPS implied, not independently verified.

netDebtToEbitda.note: FY2025=1.70x -- highest leverage of the names reviewed.

recentEvents: HEICO fiscal year ends Oct 31; TTM figures run through Jul 2026 (Q3 FY2026) per source; no FY2026 year-end results searched in this pass.
valueTrapFlags: Extremely rich valuation: trailing P/E ~55x, forward ~48x, EV/EBIT ~35x, EV/EBITDA ~30x -- priced for flawless execution.
FCF yield low (2.5%) relative to the multiple.
Highest leverage of the names reviewed: ND/EBITDA 1.56x (actual debt).
~12% unreconciled price discrepancy between two data pulls -- ratios may understate current valuation.
growthQualityNotes: Strong, consistent multi-year revenue growth: $1.87bn (FY2021) to $5.18bn TTM.
Operating margin expanded steadily: 21.1% to 24.3% TTM.
EPS growth has accelerated recently (33.5% FY2025, 31.3% TTM).
Solidly FCF positive already; concern is valuation/leverage, not growth quality.
dataGaps: Payout ratio, interest coverage not confirmed.

valuation.method: EPS-based scenario fair value off TTM EPS, explicitly reflecting the already-rich valuation and thin FCF yield

bear.note: Aerospace aftermarket demand softens, high trailing multiple compresses toward a still-rich 30x.

base.note: Continued steady double-digit growth at a multiple similar to today's, consistent with HEICO's long compounding history.

bull.note: Aftermarket and defense-electronics demand accelerates, market keeps paying a premium multiple for the quality compounding record.

valuation.whyItFits: The highest-quality, most consistent growth-and-margin-expansion track record of the whole shortlist (steady double-digit revenue growth, margin expansion every year, strong ROIC/ROE), but it is also priced for that quality -- a genuine 'pay up for quality' GARP case, not a bargain.
valuation.growthDrivers: Aftermarket aerospace parts demand, continued bolt-on M&A, Electronic Technologies defense-electronics growth.
valuation.saturation: No clear saturation signal in the data, but the valuation already assumes the compounding continues without interruption.
valuation.principalRisk: At ~55x trailing earnings with a thin FCF yield (2.5%) and the highest leverage of the shortlist, any growth disappointment would trigger an outsized multiple de-rating.
